correctness.rationale: At every positive equilibrium the infection condition reduces exactly to g(I)=k with g(I)=(1-I)ell(c+dI). Its logarithmic derivative -1/(1-I)+d/(1+exp(c+dI)) is strictly decreasing, giving all possible root counts with a unique nondegenerate interior maximum iff d>1+exp(c). The stationary equation solves via the principal positive Lambert W; its g-value is W(exp(c+d-1))/d. The actual Jacobian has negative trace and determinant -beta I g'(I), assigning saddle/sink types without unproved numerical extrapolation. DFE eigenvalues are -1 and beta(g0-k); equality is explicitly left nonhyperbolic. Rational witness is rigorous by 2<e<4 and g(1/10)>4/5. Reproduced 175 supplementary independent parameter cases using packaged standard-library Python.

value.rationale: The source develops uniqueness only under payoff monotonicity, yet increasing defection incentives make those hypotheses fail. The exact Lambert-W frontier answers a natural mathematical question: when can a locally stable disease-free equilibrium coexist with stable endemic infection under the same behavioral game? The strict, all-parameter classification and certified rational three-equilibrium witness exhibit a backward endemic regime inaccessible to a disease-free invasion test. It is an interpretable structural boundary of the dynamical model, not an arbitrary finite slice, historical-table recomputation, or just a routine code check. The anti-protective feedback assumption is explicit and limits empirical interpretation.
